TAKE IT FROM HERE

Export your groove.

Exports the full phrase and respects mute / solo. MIDI uses your DAW’s drum sounds; WAV uses this instrument’s synthesized kit. Groove timing is already written into MIDI, so applying a DAW groove again will alter it. Shaker uses GM 70 (maracas); metal hit uses GM 56 (cowbell).
INTENT BEFORE CHANCE

The method.

Pocket Lab separates three layers: genre conventions described by independent sources; authored drum studies with specific notes and defaults; and optional Livepilot-inspired production lenses. A lens changes how a study develops. It does not redefine the genre.

  1. Keep the identity. The marked anchors belong to this particular drum study. They return on generation, and locked lanes preserve your edited steps.
  2. Vary with purpose. Each study cycles through four authored motif families with related bar responses. Structure repeats after four variations; this is a bounded generator, not an unlimited model. Density adds details in chosen positions. With the lens off there is no Livepilot density ceiling; an active lens can impose its explicitly stated cap.
  3. Think in phrases. A recurring motif ties the bars together. Phrase roles are app gestures. Livepilot lenses can add subtractive development, percussion responses, evolving cells or ghost-note touch.
  4. Add a human touch. Choose eighth- or sixteenth-note swing; 50% means straight. Humanize adds repeatable timing and velocity differences, with anchor timing protected from jitter. Shared swing can still move syncopated anchors. This is not a recorded groove or a model of Dilla’s independent timing layers. Swing is bypassed for the footwork triplet and IDM quintuplet studies.

Explore the Livepilot genre library ↗
These are stylistic starting points, not universal definitions. Ambient, drone and modern classical were excluded because their source guidance favors little or no drum rhythm. No AI model, samples or Ableton connection is required. Drum sounds are synthesized in your browser. Space = play / stop · G = variation.

      What these studies can and cannot do

      Each style has four authored motif families, not an unlimited learned pattern library. Suggested tempos describe authored studies. Density ceilings and subtractive policies belong to optional Livepilot lenses; they do not define a genre. All phrases use 4/4 and one grid at a time. The footwork triplet grid cannot express every straight sixteenth alongside its triplets; the IDM quintuplet grid is one experiment.

      Humanize adds deterministic offsets, not a captured player’s groove. Preview sounds are synthesized approximations, without vocal chopping, recorded breaks, tuned basslines or signature reverb production. WAV has two identical channels. Browser-saved patterns do not sync across devices. Saved patterns keep their edits; press Generate to adopt corrected foundations.

      These links document techniques, examples and artist perspectives. They are not certifications of the generated patterns. Sources checked using Exa on 4 November 2026.
